source: Synthetic Client Requirements · Account access controls, section 3
text: Feature: Account details access. The service must authenticate users through the company identity provider and enforce role-based authorization on every account-details endpoint. Access is denied by default when the user, role, or account scope cannot be resolved. A Viewer may retrieve account details for accounts in the viewer's assigned scope but must not create, edit, or delete account settings. An Editor may update settings only within the assigned account scope. Role changes must take effect on the next authorization check; an expired or revoked session must not retain access. Acceptance checks: an in-scope Viewer can read account details; a Viewer write request is rejected with HTTP 403 and makes no change; an out-of-scope account is not disclosed; an expired session is rejected with HTTP 401; and an authorized Editor can update an in-scope setting. The client review target is 15 December 2026. Record the test result and build identifier for each acceptance check.

source: Synthetic API Specification · Create payment, POST /v1/payments
text: Operation: POST /v1/payments. Authentication: send a valid bearer access token; absent or invalid credentials receive HTTP 401. Required JSON fields: merchant_id (string), amount (positive integer in the currency's minor unit), currency (three-letter ISO 4217 code), and idempotency_key (opaque string). Reject a missing required field or invalid amount or currency with HTTP 400 and a field-level error; do not create a payment for an invalid request. A successful request returns HTTP 201 with payment_id, status, and created_at. The client must use the same idempotency_key when retrying the same logical payment. The server retains idempotency results for 24 hours; a repeated key with the same request returns the original result, while reuse with a different request is rejected. If the client times out after submission, it must check the payment status or retry with the original key, never create a new key for the same payment.

source: Synthetic Engineering Policy · Application logging and production data, sections 5-6
text: Application logs must not contain passwords, bearer tokens, authentication codes, or full payment-card data. Each request log entry must include a correlation_id so support teams can trace related events across services. Retain operational request logs for 90 days, then delete them under the approved retention process unless a documented legal hold applies. Restrict production-data access to approved personnel with a valid ticket and a documented business purpose; grant the minimum access needed and remove it when the task is complete. Report suspected exposure of credentials or customer data through the organization's incident process promptly. Do not copy production data into development or test systems unless the data-handling procedure explicitly permits an approved, protected dataset.

source: Synthetic API Specification · Retry and rate-limit behavior, section 4
text: When a response is HTTP 429, the client may retry only if the response contains a valid Retry-After header. Wait at least the indicated number of seconds before retrying and apply the service's documented backoff limits. If Retry-After is absent or invalid, do not retry automatically; surface the response for controlled handling. For a retried operation that supports idempotency, preserve the original idempotency_key across attempts. Do not automatically retry non-idempotent operations unless the endpoint specification explicitly allows it. Record the response status and request correlation identifier for troubleshooting, without logging credentials or sensitive request data.
